title: Targeting Shikimate Kinase in Acinetobacter baumannii: Gallic Acid as a Potent Inhibitory Metabolite from FDA-Approved Drug Screening
content: The current study identified certain FDA-approved drugs that could be repurposed as selective inhibitors against Acinetobacter baumannii shikimate kinase. Structure- and ligand-based drug design approaches have been integrated herein with extensive in-silico screening, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics studies, focusing on binding affinity and stability. Gallic acid, a plant-derived metabolite, has emerged as the most promising candidate, with significant binding interactions that are well supported by both computational analyses and experimental validation. MIC and MBC tests were conducted to examine their effectiveness against Acinetobacter baumannii and Enterococcus faecalis. Gallic acid demonstrated remarkable activity against the test microbial strains, presenting a promising therapeutic agent, especially given the high expression of shikimate kinase in Acinetobacter baumannii.
